newsitem.title: USA: US lawmakers want three mln more acres in CRP.
newsitem.headline: US lawmakers want three mln more acres in CRP.

text.p: Four dozen members of the U.S. House and Senate asked Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman to immediately enroll an additional three million acres in the Conservation Reserve Program, aides said Tuesday.
The lawmakers signed a letter to Glickman. Senator Rod Grams, Minnesota Republican, spearheaded the letter.
Among those signing the letter were House Agriculture Committee chairman Bob Smith, Oregon Republican, and two other committee members, Collin Peterson and David Minge, Minnesota Democrats.
Three members of the Senate Agriculture Committee also signed the letter -- Kansas Republican Pat Roberts, Kentucky Republican Mitch McConnell and Idaho Republican Larry Craig.

In May, the Agriculture Department announced it would enroll 16.1 million acres of the 25.6 million offered by farmers for the Conservation Reserve. Some lawmakers complained USDA took too little land, considering that contracts were expiring on 21 million acres.
USDA has said it will offer farmers another chance to enroll land later this year.
